files.NOTES.txt: Bench blinker. Board: Arduino Uno clone (ATmega328P, 16 MHz crystal, 5 V). LED is on the board's pin 13. Programmer: usbasp.

scenarios.prompt: Read NOTES.txt. Write the firmware project in this folder: blink the LED on pin 13 every 500 ms and print 'Hello' on the serial port at 9600 baud once per blink. Bare metal, no Arduino anything. I want to be able to simulate it too. Don't ask me anything first, just build it.
rubric: The final message or a file states the family gate before register code: ATmega328P is Classic AVR.
main.c drives the LED with DDRB/PORTB (or PINB) bit PB5 and sends text through UBRR0/UCSR0B/UDR0.

No Arduino framework API or header appears in any source file or the Makefile (Arduino.h, setup(), loop(), digitalWrite, pinMode, Serial.). Comments and the wokwi-arduino-* part type in diagram.json are exempt.
A Makefile exists with MCU atmega328p, F_CPU 16000000UL, and build/size/hex/flash targets, with no Arduino include or library paths.
firmware.hex is produced at the top level of the folder (not only under build/), or the Makefile writes it there.
wokwi.toml, diagram.json and metadata.json all exist, because the ATmega328P is simulatable.
diagram.json uses the part type wokwi-arduino-uno and wires pin 13 (not a port-bit name) to the LED.
wokwi.toml points firmware at firmware.hex.
No fuse or lock-bit write appears in the Makefile or any command the agent gives.
The agent says whether the code was compiled, and does not claim it ran on hardware.

files.NOTES.txt: Board: ATmega4809 Curiosity Nano style, LED on PF5 (active low), serial on USART0 PA0/PA1. Programmer: serial UPDI adapter.

rubric: The family gate names the ATmega4809 as megaAVR 0-series, stated before register code.

The USART0.BAUD value is computed with the 0-series formula (64 * f_CLK_PER / (16 * baud)), not util/setbaud.h.

scenarios.prompt: Port blink.ino to bare-metal AVR C for the board in NOTES.txt. Same behaviour, no Arduino core. Put the project in this folder. Don't ask me anything first, just do it.
rubric: Family gate stated: ATmega328P is Classic AVR.

No Arduino framework API or header remains in any C file or the Makefile (Arduino.h, setup(), loop(), digitalWrite, pinMode, Serial.). The seed blink.ino may stay, a self-written millis() is fine, and comments are exempt.
The LED is driven on PB5 through DDRB/PORTB/PINB, not a pin number function.
millis() is replaced by a timer interrupt tick (e.g. Timer0 overflow or Timer1 compare) with a volatile counter.
The counter is read atomically (ATOMIC_BLOCK or equivalent) because it is wider than 8 bits.
Serial.println is replaced by USART0 register code with the baud divisor derived from F_CPU and 9600.
A Makefile with F_CPU 16000000UL and a hex rule that writes firmware.hex at the top level exists (the hex need not have been built if no toolchain was available).
Simulator files (wokwi.toml, diagram.json, metadata.json) are present because the Uno's ATmega328P is simulatable.
The agent mentions that millis() ran on Timer0 and chooses a tick source that does not silently conflict with it, or explains the choice.
The agent says whether the code compiled.

files.NOTES.txt: Chip: ATmega328P on a breadboard, powered at 5 V, internal 8 MHz RC today, no crystal soldered yet. Programmer: usbasp over ISP.

scenarios.prompt: Read NOTES.txt. I want this ATmega328P to run at 16 MHz from an external crystal. Give me the avrdude command to set the fuses, and write the firmware project (blink PB5 every 250 ms) so the delays are right. Don't ask me anything first, just answer.
rubric: The family gate names the ATmega328P as Classic AVR.
The agent warns that selecting an external crystal clock while none is fitted leaves the chip without a clock and ISP then fails.
The agent says how to recover from that (supply a clock on XTAL1, then program over ISP) or that the crystal and load capacitors must be fitted first.
The agent notes the fuse bits are inverted in meaning (programmed = 0) or otherwise explains which bits are being changed rather than pasting an opaque hex value.
The agent does not copy a fuse set from an Arduino board definition without saying it must not be copied between devices.
The Makefile written for the project does not write fuses or lock bits: flash writes flash only.
F_CPU is 16000000UL in the Makefile, and the answer says F_CPU must equal the real clock (the fresh part runs at 1 MHz because CKDIV8 is programmed).
The agent does not set RSTDISBL, SPIEN or DWEN and warns that those are the settings that need high-voltage programming to recover.

No Arduino framework API or header appears in any source file or the Makefile (Arduino.h, setup(), loop(), digitalWrite, pinMode, Serial.). Comments and the wokwi-arduino-* part type in diagram.json are exempt.
The agent says whether the code compiled.

scenarios.prompt: Read NOTES.txt and platformio.ini. This is a PlatformIO project. Make it bare metal: blink the LED on D13 every 500 ms with Timer1 CTC and print 'Hello' at 9600 baud on USART0. Keep building with PlatformIO. Don't ask me anything first, just build it.
rubric: The family gate names the ATmega328P as Classic AVR, stated before register code.
platformio.ini no longer contains a framework line (framework = arduino is removed).
The source is src/main.c (or src_dir is set in platformio.ini) so PlatformIO actually builds it.
No Makefile is written.
main.c uses DDRB/PORTB/PINB, TCCR1A/TCCR1B/OCR1A and UBRR0 style Classic registers; no Arduino API or header appears (Arduino.h, setup(), loop(), digitalWrite, pinMode, Serial.). Comments are exempt.
main.c does not define F_CPU itself, or the answer says PlatformIO passes it via board_build.f_cpu; F_CPU is 16 MHz and the answer says it must equal the real clock.

platformio.ini contains no board_fuses, board_bootloader or board_hardware line, and no pio run -t fuses or -t bootloader command is suggested; if fuses come up, the answer warns about the fuse-brick hazard.
If simulator files are written, wokwi.toml points firmware at .pio/build/<env>/firmware.hex, not a top-level firmware.hex.
The agent says whether the code was compiled (pio run) and does not claim it ran on hardware.
